name: prg32-evaluation-protocol
about: How the kit measures the performance of PRG32 targets so that runs can be repeated and compared (EVAL-01, docs/evaluate.md). Changing anything here that changes a number needs a new version.

cartridge.title: PRG32 Evaluation

cases.name: clear-fill
cases.goal: clearing the screen and filling large rectangles

cartridge.same_bytes: The kit builds this source; the cartridge's SHA-256 is recorded with every run. Runs are compared only when their cartridges have the same SHA-256.

warm_up.meaning: the first runs after the cartridge is sent; recorded, never used in the statistics

repetition.prg32: the slot is selected again (POST /api/games/select): the cartridge starts from init and runs the suite once
repetition.prg32qt: the slot is selected again (POST /api/games/select): the cartridge starts from init and runs the suite once
repetition.qemu: the firmware boots again from the same staged flash image and runs the suite once

retrieval.prg32: GET /api/performance.json, every 2 seconds, until a result with a new run_id
retrieval.prg32qt: GET /api/performance.json, every 2 seconds, until a result with a new run_id
retrieval.qemu: QEMU's GDB stub, once, 30 seconds after the cartridge starts (the suite takes about 10): the broker's state, and for a finished suite the firmware's own prg32_performance_json_alloc(). The firmware is never stopped during the suite; a suite still running at that moment was disturbed, so that run is refused and the next waits twice as long. The QEMU firmware boots the stored cartridge (tools/qemu/sdkconfig.deploy), with SDL's offscreen display

timing_source.prg32: the console's microsecond timer (esp_timer), read by the cartridge with prg32_perf_now_us()
timing_source.prg32qt: PRG32-QT's clock for the cartridge, read with prg32_perf_now_us(): the host computer's time
timing_source.qemu: the emulated ESP32-C3 timer, read with prg32_perf_now_us(): it follows the host computer's clock

granularity: PRG32 performance broker ABI 1 keeps one summary per case (mean, percentiles over its frames), not every frame: one run gives one value per case and metric. The statistics are over runs.

statistics.over: the measured runs (warm-up excluded); a failed run has no values and is listed as failed
statistics.ci95: two-sided 95% Student t interval of the mean (t from the table for n - 1 degrees of freedom); none for n < 2

caveat: Times measured on an emulator (PRG32-QT, QEMU) depend on the host computer and on the emulator; they are not the times of a PRG32 console, and a faster or slower emulator run says nothing about the console. Only a prg32 target is a physical device.

dataset.csv_numbers: a dot for decimals, no thousands separator, in every interface language
